newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen property sales, industry soar in first half.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen property sales, industry soar in first half.

text.p: Property sales in China's southern boomtown of Shenzhen surged 76.5 percent year-on-year to 4.1 billion yuan ($494.5 million) in the first half of 1997, official media said on Friday.

Shenzhen saw 728,000 square metres (870,688 square yards) of property change hands in the first six months, up 56.6 percent from the same period in 1996, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said, quoting a government report.
Property analysts have said the land market in Shenzhen, a special economic zone bordering Hong Kong, slumped after peaking around 1993, and may now be on the upturn.
However, the construction area in the first six months edged down 7.0 percent to 11.5 million square metres (13.8 million square yards).
The government report also said the gross output of Shenzhen's medium and large industrial enterprises hit 27.0 billion yuan in the first six months, up 31.8 percent.
Profits of the city's industrial sector in the first five months reached 2.5 billion yuan, up 77.7 percent compared with the year-ago period, it said.
The city's bank deposits stood at 163.6 billion yuan by the end of June, up 6.9 percent from the same period in 1996.
Outstanding bank loans reached 105.8 billion yuan by end-June, up a year-on-year 3.4 percent, it said.
Retail sales rose 8.5 percent in the first half to 15.0 billion yuan, the report said.
